newsitem.title: USA: Oshkosh B'Gosh to close plant, sees Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Oshkosh B'Gosh to close plant, sees Q4 charge.

text.p: OshKosh B'Gosh Inc said Thursday it will close in early April its plant located in Oshkosh, Wis. which makes men's bib overalls.

OshKosh B'Gosh also said it is taking a $12 million pretax charge ($7.2 million or $0.60 per share after taxes) in the fourth quarter of 1996 to cover the costs of this closing and a previously announced closing of its Columbia, Ky. plant.

"It is not cost-effective for us to continue manufacturing operations when we are utilizing only one-third of the plant," said Michael Wachtel, executive vice president and chief operating officer, in a statement.

In addition, demand for men's bib overalls is not enough to justify the cost of continuing operations, even if it moves to a smaller building, he said. In the future, the men's bib overalls currently being manufactured in Oshkosh will be sourced through offshore contractors.

The plant, opened by OshKosh B'Gosh in 1985, employs about 75 people. The company plans to close the plant around April 4, 1997, at which time eligible employees will receive severance pay and outplacement assistance.
OshKosh B'Gosh said it is actively pursuing a buyer for the 91,400 square foot facility.

The write-down of assets will have no impact on the company's cash flow. "OshKosh's financial position remains strong. With over $140 million of net worth, no long-term debt and continued positive cash flow from operations, the company is well-positioned financially for the future," said David Omachinski, OshKosh B'Gosh chief financial officer, in a statement.

Excluding the Oshkosh facility, OshKosh B'Gosh operates six manufacturing plants and two distribution centers, employing over 4,700 people in the United States. Total corporate-wide employment is about 5,200 employees.
Shares of OshKosh B'Gosh, which makes and markets children's apparel, were trading off 1/4 to 13-7/8.
